title: Telling the time
goal: Ask and tell the time, read 24-hour schedules, and set the time of an appointment.

items.en: telling the time: il est trois heures

drills.explain: Heure is feminine, so one o'clock is une heure, with no s.
From two o'clock on, heures takes an s.

options: Il est quatre heures moins le quart.
Il est trois heures moins le quart.
Il est trois heures et quart.
drills.explain: 3:45 is “four o'clock minus a quarter”: quatre heures moins le quart.
With the 24-hour clock, just say the minutes as a number: no et demie.
Heures is feminine, so 21 h is vingt et une heures.

example.fr: Il est deux heures et quart.
Il est six heures et demie.
Il est cinq heures moins le quart.

items.note: Same spelling in the plural: les rendez-vous.

example.fr: Il est huit heures du soir.

blocks.title: At a French school in Montréal
blocks.context: Raj asks about the evening class. Camille works at the front desk.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Bonjour ! Le cours de français est à quelle heure, s'il vous plaît ?
lines.en: Hello! What time is the French class, please?

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Le cours du soir ? Il commence à dix-huit heures trente.
lines.en: The evening class? It starts at 18:30.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Dix-huit heures trente… Six heures et demie, c'est ça ?

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Oui, c'est ça. Et il finit à vingt et une heures.
lines.en: Yes, that's right. And it finishes at 21:00.

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Neuf heures du soir. D'accord. Et il est quelle heure maintenant ?
lines.en: Nine in the evening. OK. And what time is it now?

lines.speaker: Camille
lines.fr: Il est six heures moins le quart. Vous êtes en avance !
lines.en: It's quarter to six. You're early!

lines.speaker: Raj
lines.fr: Super ! Alors je suis à l'heure !

blocks.title: A voice message
blocks.context: Camille leaves a message for her friend Karim.
blocks.fr: Salut Karim, c'est Camille ! Rendez-vous demain à midi et demi, au café de la rue Saint-Viateur. On dîne ensemble ! À demain !
blocks.en: Hi Karim, it's Camille! Let's meet tomorrow at half past twelve, at the café on Saint-Viateur Street. We're having lunch together! See you tomorrow!

blocks.body: Notice that Camille gives the class time with the **24-hour clock** ([[dix-huit heures trente]]), and Raj checks it with the **12-hour clock** ([[six heures et demie]]). French speakers switch between the two all the time. [[À l'heure]] means *on time*; [[en retard]] means *late*.

blocks.title: Asking and telling the time
blocks.body:
Ask: [[Il est quelle heure ?]] (everyday) or [[Quelle heure est-il ?]] (a bit more formal). Both mean *What time is it?*

Answer with [[Il est]] + number + [[heure(s)]]. Always say [[heures]], even when English drops “o'clock”: *It's three* = [[Il est trois heures]].

[[Heure]] is **feminine**: [[une heure]] (1:00), then [[deux heures]], [[trois heures]]… with an *s*.

blocks.title: The 12-hour clock (conversation)
head: Time
French
rows: Il est trois heures et quart.
Il est trois heures et demie.
Il est quatre heures moins vingt.
Il est quatre heures moins le quart.
blocks.note: After half past, French usually counts **back** from the next hour with [[moins]] (minus): 3:45 = “four minus the quarter”. Say [[midi]] and [[minuit]] rather than “douze heures” in conversation. Spelling: [[et demie]] after [[heures]] (feminine), but [[midi et demi]] and [[minuit et demi]] (masculine). You will also see [[midi et demie]]; it is accepted too.

blocks.title: Morning, afternoon, evening
blocks.pattern: heure + du matin / de l'après-midi / du soir
blocks.note: With the 12-hour clock, add these to avoid confusion, like English *a.m.* and *p.m.*

examples.fr: Il est sept heures du matin.
Il est trois heures de l'après-midi.
Il est huit heures du soir.

blocks.title: The 24-hour clock (schedules, appointments)
head: Written
French
Means
blocks.note: With the 24-hour clock, minutes are **just numbers**: no [[et quart]], [[et demie]] or [[moins le quart]]. It is written with **h**: **14 h 30** (or 14:30 on screens).

blocks.title: At what time?
blocks.note: To say *at* a time, use [[à]]. To ask, use [[À quelle heure… ?]] or put [[à quelle heure]] at the end in everyday speech.

examples.fr: Le rendez-vous est à quelle heure ?
À quelle heure est le cours ?
Le rendez-vous est à quatorze heures trente.

blocks.title: Liaison with heures
blocks.body:
[[Heures]] starts with a silent *h* and a vowel sound, so numbers link to it, just like with [[ans]] and [[euros]]:

- [[une heure]] “u-n-eur”, [[deux heures]] “duh-z-eur”, [[trois heures]] “trwa-z-eur”
- [[six heures]] “see-z-eur”, [[dix heures]] “dee-z-eur”
- [[cinq heures]] “san-k-eur”, [[sept heures]] “se-t-eur”, [[huit heures]] “wee-t-eur”, [[onze heures]] “on-z-eur”
- [[neuf heures]]: the *f* becomes *v*, “nuh-v-eur”

This linking is very strong: you will always hear it.

examples.fr: Il est deux heures et demie.

blocks.body:
- **Forgetting heures:** not [[Il est trois]], but [[Il est trois heures]].
- **C'est instead of il est:** for the time, say [[Il est trois heures]], not [[C'est trois heures]]. (For *when* something happens, [[C'est à trois heures]] is fine.)
- **Un heure:** heure is feminine: [[une heure]], [[vingt et une heures]].
- **Mixing the two systems:** [[et quart]], [[et demie]] and [[moins le quart]] go with the 12-hour clock. For schedules, say [[quatorze heures trente]]; in conversation, [[deux heures et demie]].
- **Moins le quart:** don't forget [[le]] in standard French: [[cinq heures moins le quart]].

blocks.title: Time in Québec
blocks.body:
**The 24-hour clock is everywhere in writing.** Government offices, schools, clinics, transit and job schedules in Québec and in French across Canada use it: [[Le bureau ferme à 16 h 30]] (the office closes at 4:30 p.m.). The recommended way to write it in Québec and Canadian French is with spaces around **h**: **16 h 30**, **9 h**. In conversation, most people still use the 12-hour clock.

**Moins quart.** In everyday Québec speech you will often hear [[cinq heures moins quart]] without [[le]]. Understand it; in writing, use [[moins le quart]].

**Meal names.** In Québec, [[le déjeuner]] is breakfast, [[le dîner]] is **lunch** (around [[midi]]) and [[le souper]] is supper. In France, [[le petit-déjeuner]] is breakfast, [[le déjeuner]] is lunch and [[le dîner]] is the evening meal. So when a Québec colleague says [[On dîne à midi ?]], they mean lunch!

blocks.title: Listen and repeat
blocks.note: Listen for the liaison between the number and heures.

The standard spelling is [[midi et demi]], without e (midi is masculine); [[midi et demie]] is also widely seen and accepted.

blocks.prompt: Call a friend to set up a meeting. Say what time it is now, suggest a day and a time for the rendez-vous (12-hour clock), then confirm it with the 24-hour clock.
checklist: The same time with the 24-hour clock

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Salut Mei, c'est Alex ! Il est dix heures et quart. Rendez-vous demain, à deux heures et demie de l'après-midi ? Quatorze heures trente, au café. D'accord ? À demain !
models.en: Hi Mei, it's Alex! It's quarter past ten. Shall we meet tomorrow at half past two in the afternoon? 2:30 p.m., at the café. OK? See you tomorrow!

blocks.prompt: Write a short message to confirm an appointment at a clinic or an office. Give the day, the date and the time (24-hour clock), and write the time in words too.
checklist: Le rendez-vous est + day and date
à + time (24-hour clock, in digits and words)

models.label: Model answer
models.fr: Bonjour Madame Tremblay, le rendez-vous est le jeudi 12 mars, à 14 h 30 (quatorze heures trente). Merci et à bientôt ! Karim
models.en: Hello Ms. Tremblay, the appointment is on Thursday, March 12, at 2:30 p.m. Thank you and see you soon! Karim

summary:
- Ask [[Il est quelle heure ?]] / [[Quelle heure est-il ?]] and answer [[Il est trois heures]]
- Use [[et quart]], [[et demie]], [[moins le quart]], [[midi]] and [[minuit]]
- Read and say 24-hour times for schedules: [[quatorze heures trente]], [[vingt et une heures]]
- Set a time with [[à]]: [[Le rendez-vous est à midi.]], [[À quelle heure ?]]
